name: A Rock From Jezero Crater Near Perseverance
author: owlcreektech
description:
This was created using Reality Capture and three left/right Perseverance MastCam-Z images from SOL-91. Mesh reduction and texture baking done in Blender.  3D Coat was used to add PBR textures and improve texture coverage. Some areas were intetionally left smooth to indicate areas not captured by the NavCam cameras. It should also be noted that the NAVCAMs are 22cm apart so not all parallex based image pairs work well.

This technique is being used in a unique process to create textures and height maps for the Unreal Engine Landscape generator to provide rocks and other formations that are identical to those around Perseverance and Ingenuity in the upcoming VR experience "Ingenuity in VR" https://IngenuityinVR.space

Images obtained from NASA Perseverance's raw image repository

name: Mars Perseverance Landing Site - Raw Scan
author: nikska
description:
A model of the Mars Perseverance rover landing site created with raw data from NASA. 
I've first built a simple model using their Youtube stream video, but ran into compression issues. So I've just waited for the photos to finally be uploaded on Sol 4.

There are raw PNG photos available that require demosaic procedure, but those are a small subset of the available JPGs (but thise are already compressed). I've used a more abundant source of data. Hope they are going to upload more raw photos.

You can get a general inspiration for manual demosaicing using this notebook: https://github.com/colour-science/colour-demosaicing/blob/master/colour_demosaicing/examples/examples_bayer.ipynb

I've made a poor manual color correction so the images do not look so magentish. I doubt this is the right way.

All source photos are courtesy of NASA/JPL-Caltech and were downloaded from this web page: https://mars.nasa.gov/mars2020/multimedia/raw-images/

Model created with Agisoft Metashape.

name: Perseverance SOL 89 around 16:51
author: owlcreektech
description:
NASA's Perseverance model reUVed for the Unreal Engine with new 8K PBR textures.  This is also [available](https://mega.nz/folder/4rJ0FDID#hory5dJ4LLhiTGnvrka6DQ) in an 8K GLB & lighter 4K versions in both GLB and USDZ for Windows, MacOS and iOS.  It was meant to be projected at true scale so unless you have a flat surface, 10m (32.8 feet) in length, you might want to pinch & zoom as soon as it shows up in your AR viewer. In saying that if you can find an open space, it is fun to walk around Perseverance and the terrain captured using six images from the MastCam-Z cameras on SOL-89, approximately located at Long. 77.4522, Lat. 18.4439 at 16:51. More information is on the placard also showing its current and past positions over 100 Mars days from an orthographic image captured from the MRO Satellite orbiting mars in 2020.

More to come in "Ingenuity in VR" built in the Unreal Engine [https://IngenuityinVR.space](https://IngenuityinVR.space)

name: Mars SOL-116 Terrain Area with Ingenuity
author: owlcreektech
anchor_type: posición del rover en el sol; NO huella ni posición exacta del objeto
description:
Another photogrammetry based 3D terrain from images from Perseverance MastCam-Z on SOL 116.  Ingenuity was added, but prettys sure it never took off from this location.

Techncial Notes:
I have been testing Apple's new photogrammetry API in Mac OS 12 with good results & minimal work; especillay if using an iPhone. However an iOS device is not needed as Apple would lead you to believe & any set of overlapping images will work. The terrain here has a few problems, but this has more to do with the way Perseverance captures images for 2D mosaics, & not for photogrammetry.  Regardless, it takes longer to select & scrape the images off the web, than to run the 'Object Capture' test CLI app.

I also like it because it gives you basic PBR textures sans Metallic or Emission but those are easy to add. Here, there are only a few areas that may have metal (mainly oxide). I did however create emission, subsurface & specular textures to add more depth & illumination to the sand and I will start testing 800nm images soon.

name: "Bored" Rock on SOL-190
author: owlcreektech
description:
On S**OL-190, Perseverance** made its second attempt to bore a geologiy sample, but this time selecting a more structurally sound geological speciman. It appears Perserverance was sucessful.  Look forward to seeing what its composition is. 

As with the other Mars terrain meshes availalbe in this account, Unreal Engine, Reality Capture was used with two specially prepared left/right stereo images (4) from Perseverance's NavCam.  The final texture created was used in Paint.Net (& plugins) to create four PBR textures: Roughness, Metallic, Specular and Normal.  These were brought in, along with a flipped difused texture after the model was imported to allow for PNGs higher fidelity.

This model is free, but please credit 'Owl Creek Technologies' and "NASA JPL' if you plan to use these in your own project or presentation.

name: "Rochette" drilled for the 2nd time on SOL-196
author: owlcreektech
description:
**NASA JPL** decided to drill a second time into the rock nicknamed "Rochette" due to its unique geologic makeup, which includes salt minerals making it a good candidate as it's a good indicator of water, more important -- life.  

This model was created using 32 left/right Perseverance NAVCAM images, assembled into a mosaic and color graded using a "grey balance" process, then processed by Reality Capture to derive the 3D mesh and 8K texture. Further mesh decimation/refinement & re-UVEd in Blender 3.0 Alpha and then brought into 3D Coat to project 2D textures captured by the Watson camera of Rochette.  The cloning tool was used to fill in areas not available from other images.  SM4 Pro was used to create PBR textures for enhancing the surfaces and finally bringing in the animated Perseverance's drilling arm to reenact the process taken to create the 27mm holes in the rock.

Note:  Please provide credit to NASA JPL and Owl Creek Technologies if you choose to use the model in your own product or presentation

name: Kodiak Butte, Jezero crater (Mars)
author: LPG-3D
description:
This is a Digital Outcrop Model of the Kodiak Butte, situated south of the main delta front in the Jezero crater (Mars).
The model is the result of an imaging experiment aiming at reconstructing 3D models using long-distance individual frames taken using the 563-mm Remote Micro Imager telescope of the SuperCam instrument onboard the M2020 Perseverance rover.

This model was computed using images taken during sols 63 and 248 from between 2 and 2.5 km away from the butte during the early exploration of the crater floor unit.

This is the very first result at producing a 3D model using long-distance RMI imagery in Jezero, allowing to observe the characteristic geometry of pro-delta deposits within the butte.

Data illustrating the “Flow direction assessed from the 3D geometry reconstruction of the Kodiak butte in jezero crater (Mars)" abstract for the 53rd LPSC conference (march 2022),[ available here](https://www.hou.usra.edu/meetings/lpsc2022/pdf/1189.pdf).

Model by Gwénaël Caravaca.

name: Rockytop top (Mars)
author: LPG-3D
description:
This model represents the surface top of the Rockytop area (Jezero crater), the uppermost member of the basal Shenandoah formation that contains the basal layers of Jezero's delta.
It was imaged by the *Ingenuity* helicopter during its flights 41 and 42. As a reconnaissance tool for the Mars 2020 rover *Perseverance*, *Ingenuity* flew above the Rockytop area to recon the terrain a few Sols (martian days) before the rover actually drove by this place during its ascent of Jezero's delta (~Feb. 16th, 2023).

On this small patch, we can observe rubbles of smooth, fine-grained sediments, probably laid down in a calm shallow fluvial context. These sediments show contorted structures, probably due to soft sediment deformation (?).

Model made from 18 RTE images. Raw images are available at https://mars.nasa.gov/mars2020/multimedia/raw-images/. Image treatment and colorimetric corrections were done by Thomas Appéré and visible at https://www.flickr.com/photos/thomasappere/

Model by G. Caravaca

name: M2020 Zcam -- Sample Depot VR environment
author: Mastcam-Z
description: Immerse yourself in the 3D depiction of the "Sample Depot" nestled within the intriguing Jezero Crater on Mars. Engage with each individual sample tube to unravel its unique origin story. The Perseverance rover meticulously placed ten such tubes in this Martian flatland, earmarked for an exciting future endeavor: the Mars Sample Return Mission. Housed within these tubes are precious pieces of Mars - rocks, regolith, and atmospheric samples - carefully collected throughout the rover's industrious initial years on the Red Planet. To simplify their origin, the boxes beneath each sample are color-coded: red signifies samples from Séítah, blue marks those from the delta front, while green encapsulates all other regions, including one intriguing sample from the Octavia E. Butler landing site and another from the vicinity of Séítah.
